title: TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours Expiry Extensions and the Extension Order Form
content:
Every extension of a TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block is bought on the authorized contact's signed order form. The fee of such an extension is figured under the extension fee basis, rounded half up to the cent, and is invoiced when the extension takes effect on that signature. A block whose hours were rolled out still cannot be extended.

## When the fee is worked out

The extension fee is fixed only after the block's hours ledger carries the remote-support draw of the client's ticket most recently resolved to the prepaid-block route with remote labor.

The extension fee is not worked out until the block's hours ledger carries the onsite-support draw of the client's ticket most recently resolved to the prepaid-block route with onsite labor, where that visit is an installation visit.

Before the extension fee is worked out for a client holding exactly one live time-and-materials engagement, one signed and not yet accepted, closed or cancelled, the block's hours ledger must carry the project-work draws of every group of the client's most recently dated project time logged to the prepaid-block route, a group being that date's lines of one level; for any other client the extension fee does not wait on project time.

Each of these is a state of the block's hours ledger; the fee quoted is the one worked out once the ledger shows the states that apply to the client.

## The extension form: `sign_block_extension_cebc1113`

**Capability.** The client's authorized contact e-signs an extension order form for one TimeBank block at the quoted fee. Signing books the extension form as signed, moves the block's expiry date to the new date, counts one more extension on the block and posts the extension fee invoice dated today. The contact sees the signed form, the later expiry date on the block and the fee invoice on the account.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, the authorized contact giving the e-signature.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The client reference number of the organisation the block belongs to, as returned by the client profile lookup. |
| `timebank_block_id` | The reference number of the TimeBank block being extended, as returned by the TimeBank block lookup. |
| `new_expiry_date` | The block's last valid day after the extension, YYYY-MM-DD, US Eastern calendar date. |
| `quoted_amount_usd` | The extension fee quoted on the form, in USD with 2 decimal places, a positive amount rounded half up to the cent before it is passed. |

**Return.** `order_reference` (reference of the signed extension form), `block_reference` (the block extended), `new_expiry_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `extension_count` (extensions now applied to the block), `quoted_amount_usd` (USD with 2 decimal places), `invoice_number` (INV- followed by 6 digits) and `invoice_posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, today). The `order_reference` and `invoice_number` confirm the extension was signed and invoiced.
